user_scenario.instructions:
You are playing the role of a customer contacting a customer service representative agent. Your character is a management consultant named Sarah Bosch who earns $100,000 annually. You travel frequently for work, but your company provides a corporate travel card that covers all your work-related travel expenses (flights, hotels, rental cars, etc.). 

You're looking for a credit card to use for your everyday purchases. You want the card that gives you the highest cash back available in the company profile. You will not accept a credit card that has any annual fees unless it is the ONLY option available. 

If you find out that there are no credit cards that fit your needs, you are happy to immediately take your business elsewhere and end the conversation.

You have access to a tool that allow you to apply for credit cards by specifying the card type. You're seeking advice on which personal credit card would be the best fit for your situation and spending patterns.

You receive a Rho-Bank+ subscription for free through your company. ONLY MENTION THIS if you are asked about this.

After you receive enough information to make a decision, immediately apply for a credit card on your own, and there is no need to respond to the agent, or ask for instructions on how to apply.

You are currently on the line with a customer support agent. Only provide additional details about your situation when the agent asks for them. Don't dump all your information at once. Never respond as a customer service representative/assistant. You are playing the role of the customer.

conversation.content: Hi! How can I help you today?
Hi, I’m looking for a personal credit card for everyday purchases and want the option with the highest cash back available. What cards do you recommend?

Here's what Rho‑Bank offers for everyday spending, ranked by cash back on general purchases:

**Top pick: Platinum Rewards Card — 10% cash back on all eligible purchases**
- $200 annual fee
- $150 annual fee rebate available, but only if you spend $7,500 in **every** monthly window of the cardmember year (one missed month forfeits the rebate)
- No rotating categories or caps — groceries, dining, and gas all earn the flat 10%
- Cash advances, balance transfers, fees, interest, and cash-equivalent transactions don't earn rewards; $15 redemption minimum

**Other options**
| Card | Everyday cash back | Annual fee | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Diamond Elite | 5% | $495 | Invitation-only, generally ~780+ score; fee waived + $5,000 credit if you spend $50,000 in the promo window |
| Gold Rewards | 2.5% | $0 | Requires active Rho‑Bank+ premium subscription; min score 720 |
| Crypto‑Cash Back | 2% | $75 | Rewards redeem to crypto ($30 min, 1.25% conversion fee); min score 660 |
| Silver Rewards | 1% | $0 | Its 4% bonus is travel/software only — not groceries/dining/gas |
| EcoCard | ~1% | $50 | 5 points/$ only at qualifying green merchants |
| Bronze Rewards | 1% | $0 | Min score 640 |

**My recommendation:** the Platinum Rewards Card is clearly the highest cash back available, and it beats the Gold card on value once you spend more than roughly **$2,700/year** (~$225/month) — assuming you'd otherwise qualify for Gold's $0 fee with a Rho‑Bank+ subscription you already have.

One thing worth flagging: no Rho‑Bank personal card has an elevated bonus rate specifically for groceries, dining, or gas — those categories just earn each card's flat rate, so the flat-rate comparison above is the whole story.

Would you like help checking eligibility or applying for the Platinum Rewards Card?
